The company states that it differentiates itself by supplying quality American-made products at an affordable price.

about:

The company creates hyperlocal graphics that honor the history and traditions of colleges, universities, resorts, camps, and military organizations. Its product lines include custom apparel, stickers laminated with a scratch‑resistant textured matte finish, canvas prints, wood blocks, photo frames, coasters, and ornaments. Processes span graphic design, apparel manufacturing, sticker printing and lamination, canvas printing, and production of wood, photo, and ceramic home‑decor items. No facility size, headcount, or annual volume figures are published.

Image One serves collegiate buyers of licensed apparel, resort operators seeking region‑specific souvenirs, summer camps, church camps, day camps, and military units. The company emphasizes designs that capture local traditions for each client type, such as graphics tailored to a resort’s services or a camp’s focus.

The firm positions its differentiation on hyperlocal graphics that bridge tradition and contemporary trends, backed by more than three decades of apparel experience. It also highlights the durability of its stickers, which feature a textured matte lamination that resists fading, water, and scratches on surfaces ranging from vehicle windows to laptops.

name: Imricor Medical Systems
old_description: Imricor was co-founded by Steve Wedan in 2006 and along with three Imricor pioneers established in the Twin Cities area. Imricor has quickly grown to be the first and only company in the world to bring commercially viable and safe iCMR products to the catheter ablation market. As Imricor continues to grow and develop this market, its focus is and remains the improvement of ablation therapy for patients all around the world.
about:
Imricor Medical Systems was co-founded by Steve Wedan in 2006 and established in the Twin Cities area, with its headquarters in Burnsville, Minnesota. The company began with Wedan and three other pioneers aiming to bring interventional magnetic resonance (iMR) technology to the catheter ablation market. It is publicly traded on the Australian Securities Exchange (ASX:IMR).

The company develops and manufactures MR-compatible products for interventional MR procedures, including capital equipment such as the NorthStar Mapping System and the Advantage-MR EP Recorder/Stimulator, as well as single-use devices like the Vision-MR Ablation Catheter 2.0, Vision-MR Diagnostic Catheter, and steerable sheaths. Operations are based in a Burnsville facility housing research, development, quality, and commercial teams.

Imricor serves the cardiac ablation, electrophysiology, and interventional cardiology markets, supplying hospitals and cardiac centers worldwide. Early commercial customers include Dresden Heart Centre in Germany, Rady Children's Hospital in San Diego, Amsterdam UMC, Lausanne University Hospital in Switzerland, and Haga Hospital in the Netherlands. Distribution partnerships extend to Philips, GE HealthCare, and Regional Health Care Group for Australia and New Zealand.

The company was founded to replace x-ray fluoroscopy with real-time MR guidance during cardiac ablation, leveraging MRI's superior soft-tissue imaging to improve procedural safety and efficacy. Its stated mission remains the improvement of ablation therapy for patients globally, supported by CE Mark approvals in Europe, TGA approval in Australia, and FDA clearance for select products in the United States.

name: Imtron Electronics
old_description: Minnesota-based Imtron has supplied high-quality electronic components to manufacturers across the world since 1988.
about:
Imtron Electronics, based in Eden Prairie, Minnesota, has been supplying electronic components since its founding in 1988. The company operates as a stocking distributor and is led by President and General Manager Jeff Spaeth alongside a small team of sales and operations professionals.

The distributor stocks a range of connectors, crystals, thermal-management products, and power supplies from partners such as LEMO, Magtech, TXC, Henkel, and Mornsun. Imtron maintains inventory to serve global customers and emphasizes a consultative approach to help engineers select components for applications where failure is not an option.

Its customer base spans the automotive, aviation, medical, and military sectors. The company’s blog and marketing materials highlight work with medical-grade electronics manufacturers and defense programs that require rugged, compliant components.

Imtron says its differentiation lies in decades of component-sales experience, ISO 9001:2015 certification, and a focus on supplying parts that “cannot fail in the field,” backed by technical consultation and long-term supplier relationships.

name: In La Apparel
old_description: Apparel Branders Inc. sewing department specializes in apparel manufacturing. Every stage of garment construction is meticulously assembled, closely supervised and must comply with strict quality guidelines. Our quality control system is designed to yield a defect-free garment that matches your exact specifications. We have a variety of machines and techniques to accommodate many different types of sewing operations.
about:
In La Apparel operates from Los Angeles and Orange County, California, as a vertically integrated apparel manufacturer focused on made-in-USA production. The company runs two factories, including a knitting mill in the Los Angeles fashion district, and employs a small team to manage design, development, and production for private-label clients.

The company provides full-service private-label manufacturing covering design consulting, pattern making, grading, marking, cutting, sewing, fabric and garment dyeing, printing, embroidery, sublimation, heat transfer, and specialty decorations such as deboss, burnout, and reflective transfers. Its in-house knitting mill produces fabrics in cotton, synthetic, viscose/modal, polyester, melanges, organic, and slub yarns, while also offering organic and sustainable options. Production scales from low-minimum-order samples to large-volume runs, with packaging and fulfillment handled on-site.

Clients span the fashion industry, corporate and uniform programs, promotional products, and entertainment production studios creating costumes for motion pictures, commercials, and television. The company works directly with independent designers, established brands, and artists, offering end-to-end development from concept through retail-ready shipment.

In La Apparel differentiates itself through a sweatshop-free, vertically integrated model that keeps all manufacturing domestic, emphasizing customer service and quality control at every stage. The firm highlights its 'Organic Zone' for 100% organic apparel, fast turnaround times, and the ability to process orders of any quantity, positioning itself as a one-stop partner from fabric development to final delivery.

name: Index Packaging, Inc.
old_description: Index Packaging’s manufacturing facility in Milton, New Hampshire specializes in wood packaging products, including wood crates and wood pallets, both new and recycled. Since we control the entire production process and have our own fleet of vehicles serving New England, we can guarantee your order will be on time.
about:
Index Packaging, Inc. was founded in 1968 by Bill and Connie Lander in the basement of their New York home. The company moved to Milton, New Hampshire in 1981 and remains a closely held, family‑owned corporation now led by second‑generation shareholders including Bruce Lander, Debora Lussier, and Connie Lander. From its start as a small packaging operation, it has grown into a midsize manufacturer with four production and warehouse campuses across New Hampshire.

The company designs and manufactures custom packaging for fragile or high‑value items, producing foam inserts, corrugated boxes, wood crates and pallets, and specialty shippers such as apple gift boxes. All three material streams—foam, wood, and corrugated—are processed under one roof across facilities totaling more than 275,000 square feet. In‑house capabilities include design and engineering, prototyping, CNC foam fabrication, corrugated converting, wood crate assembly, kiln‑drying to ISPM‑15 standards, vendor‑managed inventory, warehousing, and a dedicated trucking fleet for New England delivery plus nationwide LTL and parcel shipping. The operation employs over 200 people.

Index Packaging serves industrial equipment manufacturers, military and defense contractors, medical and pharmaceutical companies, laboratories, and food and agriculture businesses. Concrete examples include custom crates for sensitive instrumentation, foam‑filled shippers for fruit and produce, and protective packaging for cell‑phone and electronics shipments.

The business was built on a “Protection by Design” philosophy that emphasizes service, quality, and quick decision‑making enabled by its family ownership. An internal recycling program diverts polyurethane and polyethylene foam, corrugated scrap, and wood waste into secondary markets, and the company’s own logistics network allows it to guarantee on‑time delivery throughout New England.
